items.note: Within-participants study of design students using an AI creativity support tool (SketchifAI) with text, sketch, or sketch-plus-tags prompts, scoring divergent thinking (fluency, variety, originality, quality); AI-configuration comparison only, N and order randomization not stated; arXiv 2606.26626 is the same paper.

Quasi-experiment with 62 pre-service teachers comparing concept mapping plus generative AI (n=30) with standalone generative AI (n=32) on digital storytelling outcomes, including an 'innovation' dimension; AI-configuration comparison, non-random.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page all failed); search notes say 566 conservatory students in a ChatGPT intervention vs control group with Torrance tests pre and post, allocation unknown; TTCT is a test without AI, so this may be an after_ai outcome.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect all failed); search notes say college students with and without ChatGPT support were compared on creative problem-solving performance across stages, with mentor interviews on idea homogenization; design and N unverified.

ECER 2025 conference abstract: 86 media art students randomly allocated to AI training plus generative tools (n=29), AI training plus non-AI digital tools (n=28), or a control class (n=29), then made animation materials; reports no creativity gain from generative AI, but it is unclear whether creativity was scored on the animation output or measured as a mindset scale.

Two empirical studies compare text, image, and 3D generative models in supporting combinational design ideation; the abstract does not say whether human designers worked under different AI conditions or how ideation was scored, so it may be model-only or a system exploration.

Design case study comparing co-ideation with a custom GPT (Co-Ideator framework) against traditional ideation and a no-AI condition, with novelty and quality of ideas higher with the custom GPT; abstract gives no N (search notes say 48) or assignment method.

Novice programmers using a CPS-integrated ChatGPT assistant (CPS-GPT) outperformed a comparison condition (likely conventional ChatGPT) on creativity (d=.557) and other outcomes; N, assignment, and whether creativity is a scored output or a self-report scale are not in the abstract.

System paper (Reflexa, an LLM reflection scaffold for creative coding) with a within-subject study of 18 participants reporting higher originality and aesthetic quality; the comparison condition is not described, so it may lack a comparison arm (possible system_paper_no_comparison); below 50 participants.

Quasi-experiment with 120 music students in Guangdong: AI-assisted composition tools vs control, compositions rated pre and post on nine dimensions including creative fluency; the abstract does not say whether the tools are generative AI or whether AI was available at posttest.
